name: NC Land and Water Fund Restoration Program

funder.name: North Carolina Land and Water Fund

summary: North Carolina state grants for restoring streams, wetlands (including peat and pocosin wetlands), floodplains and living shorelines, and for removing dams and culverts, led by conservation nonprofits, local governments or state agencies.

status.quote: Subscribe to our email list at the bottom of this page to get annual grant cycle announcements.

recurring.quote: January 15 - Grant Cycle Opens. The application web-forms and updated funding manuals will be available on our website. Please plan to update your copy of the Funding Manual after the cycle opens. March 1 - Application Deadline.

status.quote: Application forms can be accessed via https://nclwf.nc.gov/apply and are available January 15, 2026. Applications must be submitted by midnight on March 1, 2026.

opens.quote: Application forms can be accessed via https://nclwf.nc.gov/apply and are available January 15, 2026.

deadline.quote: Applications must be submitted by midnight on March 1, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: the applicant must be either: a State agency; a local government unit; or a nonprofit corporation whose primary purpose is the conservation, preservation, and/or restoration of our State's cultural, environmental, and natural resources.

geography.quote: a nonprofit corporation whose primary purpose is the conservation, preservation, and restoration of North Carolina's natural and cultural resources is eligible to apply for a grant

access.quote: Grants are accepted through an online webform program.

window.quote: The North Carolina Land and Water Fund has one grant cycle per year for the Acquisition, Restoration, Planning and Innovative Stormwater programs.

co_finance_required.quote: Are matching funds required? No, but matching funds are considered in the Application Rating System and projects with little or no match are rarely funded.
